title: Trump Nominates Budget Deputy for Nonpartisan Federal Watchdog Role

Trump Nominates Budget Deputy for Nonpartisan Federal Watchdog Role
The move could put a top administration official in charge of an oversight agency that has faulted the White House for past violations of the law.
President Trump on Monday nominated Eric M. Ueland, a top deputy at the White House budget office, to serve as the nation’s comptroller general, a move that could hand control of a nonpartisan federal watchdog to one of the administration’s political allies.
If confirmed by the Senate, Mr. Ueland would assume the leadership of the Government Accountability Office, an agency whose responsibilities include monitoring federal spending, identifying government waste and ensuring that the executive branch complies with the wishes of Congress. The post carries a 15-year term.
The selection of Mr. Ueland quickly evoked furious opposition from top congressional Democrats, who accused Mr. Trump of trying to neuter legislative oversight just weeks before Republicans are set to surrender control of Congress.
Mr. Ueland currently serves under Russell T. Vought, the director of the White House Office of Management and Budget, which has worked on behalf of Mr. Trump to block billions of dollars in spending and fire droves of civil workers, often without the explicit approval of Congress. Frequently, the office known as G.A.O. has found some of those activities to be illegal.
The problems date back to the president’s first term, when the accountability office concluded in 2020 that the White House had wrongly withheld nearly $400 million in military assistance to Ukraine. Congressional Democrats would later cite that finding when they commenced a push to impeach Mr. Trump.
But the violations have continued into Mr. Trump’s second stint in office. Repeatedly, the G.A.O. has found that the budget office, where Mr. Ueland is deputy director, has illegally withheld congressionally enacted funds in spite of laws that prohibit the practice, which is known as impoundment
